feat(teacher): room content editor

The biggest hole in the product: a teacher could create a room and then
never put anything in it. POST /rooms/:id/tasks, PATCH, DELETE and
GET /rooms/:id/edit all existed on the API and nothing in the frontend
called any of them, so every room reached learners empty and no room
could honestly be published.

/teacher/rooms/[id] now edits a room's content:

- Tasks: title, duration, XP, reorder by position, add and delete.
- Lesson sections per task: optional heading, body, and a bullet list
  entered one per line.
- Questions per task: single choice, true/false and short answer.
  Switching to true/false writes its own option pair; marking a correct
  option in a single-answer question clears the others, because the
  server rejects any other shape.
- Short answers take accepted values one per line, matched
  case-insensitively server-side.

Client-side validation mirrors RoomsService.createQuestion exactly, so a
teacher sees "at least two options" next to the field instead of a 400
after pressing save. Saving a task sends it whole, which is what the
upsert endpoint expects - it replaces questions wholesale so the editor
can reorder freely.

The room list links to it per row, and the create form now says what
the next step is rather than implying the room is finished.

fix(catalog): let teachers add modules to published paths

A regression I introduced with the F-02 ownership guard. createModule
required ownership of the destination path, but curriculum paths are
generally admin-authored, so in practice a teacher could only ever build
under a path they had created themselves - the module form in the
teacher console offers every visible path and each one would have
answered 403.

Attaching is now governed by the rule RoomsService already applies to
modules: a published path is public structure and open to
contributions, an unpublished one is somebody's unreviewed draft and
stays closed. Re-parenting follows the same rule.

The security property is unchanged - a teacher still cannot inject
content into an unreviewed draft, and still cannot edit or publish a
path they do not own.

fix(dashboard): stop a cold backend from looking like a failed login

The dashboard was unreachable in a way that looked exactly like login
being broken, and it was a redirect loop:

  1. the page called /profiles/me through apiFetchOrNull, which returns
     null for *any* failure - including a timeout;
  2. null was read as "not signed in", so the page redirected to /login;
  3. proxy.ts looked at the Supabase cookie, found a perfectly good
     session, and redirected straight back to /dashboard;
  4. repeat.

The trigger is the free Render plan: it parks the instance after 15
minutes and takes tens of seconds to wake, so the first request after a
quiet spell fails through nobody's fault.

- requireProfile (lib/api/viewer.ts) replaces the null check on the four
  gated pages. Only a real 401/403 goes to /login; a timeout or a 502
  while the instance wakes is re-thrown for error.tsx, which explains
  itself and offers a retry instead of bouncing in circles.
- Both API clients now bound each attempt at 15s and retry twice, with
  backoff, on the statuses a proxy returns while something behind it is
  starting. Reads only: replaying a POST could submit an answer or
  create a room twice, and 429 is excluded because retrying a rate limit
  is the opposite of the right response.
- apiFetchOrNull keeps swallowing everything and is now documented as
  being for optional panels only, with a note not to use it to decide
  whether somebody is signed in.

feat(auth): resend the confirmation e-mail

Supabase mails a confirmation link once per sign-up. If it never
arrives - spam folder, wrong address, an expired link, or the built-in
SMTP's project-wide hourly cap - there was nothing the visitor could
do: signing up again with a known address is answered without sending
anything, deliberately, so the form cannot be used to test which
addresses are registered.

A resend button now appears in the two places we know the address is
registered but unconfirmed: after a sign-up that needs confirmation,
and after a sign-in that fails with "email not confirmed". It calls
auth.resend({ type: "signup" }) with emailRedirectTo built from
getSiteUrl(), and when Supabase answers "you can only request this
after N seconds" it counts N down on the button instead of letting
people press something guaranteed to fail.

The expired-link message no longer tells people to register again -
a new link is one sign-in attempt away now.

docs/auth-emails.md explains the three separate reasons a link appears
to arrive only once, and which of them are dashboard settings: the
built-in SMTP is capped per project and Supabase calls it test-only, so
production needs a custom SMTP provider. That part cannot be fixed in
code.

fix(auth): fall back to Vercel's production domain for the site URL

getSiteUrl threw in production whenever NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL was unset,
which turns a forgotten dashboard setting into broken sign-up, broken
e-mail confirmation and a broken password reset. The frontend is not
running this code yet, so nothing is live-broken - but deploying it as
written would have done exactly that.

It now falls back to VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL (and the
NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant the client bundle sees), which Vercel sets from
the build system rather than from a request. That keeps the property
the throw was protecting: the redirect origin is still never derived
from attacker-controllable input. Explicit configuration still wins,
and off-platform production still throws rather than guessing.

Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL explicitly once there is a custom domain - the
Vercel variable keeps pointing at the *.vercel.app one.

fix(deploy): run migrations in the build, and put the risky one last

Two ordering problems, both of which the 12 Sep outage exposed.

Migrations now run in the Render build command, before the compile, and
are allowed to fail it. A failed build leaves the previous deploy
serving traffic, so the schema can never end up behind the code that
reads it - which is precisely what happened when PR #9 merged and the
new code went looking for profiles.deleted_at.

They were excluded until now because the schema was applied to Supabase
by hand, so `migrate deploy` would try to replay the init migration and
hit "relation already exists". prisma/deploy.mjs handles that: it
inspects the database and either baselines the two hand-applied
migrations and deploys the rest, builds a fresh schema, or just deploys
what is pending. Idempotent. prisma:baseline also now covers the second
hand-applied migration, which it had been missing.

20260911000100_answer_attempt_idempotency is renumbered to …000500 so
it runs LAST. It is the only migration that can fail on existing data
(duplicate correct attempts block the unique index), and at …000100 it
sat in front of account_deletion - so a duplicate row would have
stopped deleted_at from ever being created and left the API down. Last
means a failure there costs only the F-04 fix.

fix(deps): align @nestjs/common with core, and check the app actually boots

My npm audit fix in 1285723 moved @nestjs/core and platform-express

fix(security): per-request CSP nonce instead of 'unsafe-inline' scripts

The Report-Only CSP shipped with script-src 'unsafe-inline', which
neuters the one directive that matters against XSS. The proxy now mints
a nonce per response, hands it to Next.js through the x-nonce and CSP
request headers (which is how App Router stamps its own inline
bootstrap scripts), and sets the same policy on the response. script-src
is 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic', with 'unsafe-eval' only in
development for React Refresh.

The static CSP is removed from next.config.ts: two policies are
intersected by the browser and would have broken the nonced scripts.
Styles stay on 'unsafe-inline' - Tailwind and framer-motion set style
attributes that nonces cannot cover, and that is a far smaller surface.

Still Report-Only until the violation log has been reviewed.

fix(security): frontend security headers and Secure session cookies

F-08 and the cookie report.

next.config.ts had no headers() block at all. Adds HSTS, nosniff,

as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only so the violation log decides when
it can be enforced. connect-src is derived from the configured Supabase

Cookies, deliberately narrower than the cookie report recommended:
